name: Hill & Knowlton

summary.text: Hill & Knowlton is a public relations firm that was owned by WPP and, in 2024, merged with Burson Cohn & Wolfe to form Burson. In 1990–91 it was the principal contractor of Citizens for a Free Kuwait, a group established and almost entirely funded by the Kuwaiti government after the Iraqi invasion to build American support for military action. Of $11.9 million the Kuwaiti government channeled to the group, $10.8 million went to Hill & Knowlton in fees. The firm introduced a 15-year-old witness identified only as Nayirah to the Congressional Human Rights Caucus on October 10, 1990, where she testified that she saw Iraqi soldiers remove babies from incubators; in 1992 she was identified as the daughter of Kuwait's ambassador to the United States, and later investigations could not substantiate her account.

sources.publisher: PR Watch / Center for Media and Democracy (Stauber & Rampton, Toxic Sludge Is Good for You)
sources.title: How PR Sold the War in the Persian Gulf

facts.claim: Citizens for a Free Kuwait was established by the Kuwaiti government to persuade the American public to support US military action in the Persian Gulf; its principal payment went to Hill & Knowlton.
facts.quote: Citizens for a Free Kuwait (CFK) was an astroturf operation established by the Kuwaiti government to persuade the American public to look favourably at US military action in the Persian Gulf. Its principal payment was to public relations firm Hill & Knowlton

sources.publisher: PR Watch / Center for Media and Democracy (Stauber & Rampton, Toxic Sludge Is Good for You)
sources.title: How PR Sold the War in the Persian Gulf

facts.claim: Over roughly six months starting nine days after the invasion, the Kuwaiti government channeled $11.9 million to Citizens for a Free Kuwait, whose only other funding totalled $17,861 from 78 individuals; $10.8 million of the group's budget went to Hill & Knowlton as fees.
facts.quote: Over the next six months, the Kuwaiti government channeled $11.9 million dollars to Citizens for a Free Kuwait, whose only other funding totalled $17,861 from 78 individuals. Virtually all of CFK's budget -- $10.8 million -- went to Hill & Knowlton in the form of fees.

sources.publisher: PR Watch / Center for Media and Democracy (Stauber & Rampton, Toxic Sludge Is Good for You)
sources.title: How PR Sold the War in the Persian Gulf

facts.claim: On October 10, 1990, a 15-year-old Kuwaiti girl identified only as Nayirah testified before the Congressional Human Rights Caucus that she had seen Iraqi soldiers take babies from incubators; Hill & Knowlton, working with Representatives Tom Lantos and John Porter, introduced her at the hearing.
facts.quote: Hill & Knowlton, in coordination with Congressmen Tom Lantos and John Porter, introduced her at that hearing.

sources.publisher: PR Watch / Center for Media and Democracy (Stauber & Rampton, Toxic Sludge Is Good for You)
sources.title: How PR Sold the War in the Persian Gulf
A Debate on One of the Most Frequently Cited Justifications for the 1991 Persian Gulf War: Did PR Firm Hill & Knowlton Invent the Story of Iraqi Soldiers Pulling Kuwaiti Babies From Incubators?

facts.claim: In January 1992 it was reported that Nayirah was the daughter of Saud Nasir al-Sabah, Kuwait's ambassador to the United States, and that she had received coaching from Hill & Knowlton before testifying; John MacArthur's book Second Front states the firm prepared her for the presentation.
facts.quote: Nayirah was revealed to be Nayirah al-Ṣabah, daughter of Kuwait's ambassador to the United States, Saud Nasser al-Sabah, who had not been in Kuwait during the invasion but was in the U.S. receiving coaching from Hill & Knowlton

sources.publisher: PR Watch / Center for Media and Democracy (Stauber & Rampton, Toxic Sludge Is Good for You)
sources.title: How PR Sold the War in the Persian Gulf

facts.claim: Later investigations by human rights organizations could not find that Nayirah had any connection to the hospital, and an ABC News report found that Iraqi troops almost certainly had not stolen hospital incubators and left hundreds of Kuwaiti babies to die.
facts.quote: An ABC News report found that Iraqi troops "almost certainly had not stolen hospital incubators and left hundreds of Kuwaiti babies to die."

facts.claim: Citizens for a Free Kuwait provided office space to the Congressional Human Rights Caucus at a reduced rate, and a Hill & Knowlton vice president helped organize the congressional hearings.

openQuestions: Amnesty International's 1991 retraction of its December 1990 report on the incubator allegations (which the site mentions) was described only in secondary and opinion sources; locate Amnesty's own statement before citing it.
Hill & Knowlton's FARA registration for Citizens for a Free Kuwait was not located; it would confirm the fee figures from a primary record.
Fee figures vary ($10.7 million, $10.8 million, $11.85 million for the government total); the $10.8 million figure is from Stauber and Rampton's account.
